question.problem: Let $A$ be a $m \times n$ matrix. What is the image of $\text{Col}(A^T)$ under the action of $A?$
question.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ by $A$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154359/assets/dc853850b03dd2cf8fcf0168392e3490423725120b6acb55f88028a702d30fa5.svg)

Therefore, the image of $\mathbb{R}^n$ under the action of $A$ must be $\text{Col}(A),$ the column space of $A.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(A)$ is mapped to the zero vector $\mathbf{0}$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}(A^T)$ must be $\text{Col}(A).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154359/assets/8b08bdf79d53f312cabd665bcd4669795bd8851dfb33d5e5db6178bd80b24398.png)
